notes: Moon: NASA does not publish center coordinates for Artemis III regions; each is anchored on the IAU feature of the same name (USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature). Mars: published landing coordinates.

targets.name: Haworth rim
targets.why: Rim of a permanently shadowed crater near the south pole; candidate landing region with access to cold traps.

anchor.note: Approximate: ring on the rim of IAU crater Haworth (D = 51.4 km).

targets.name: Malapert Massif
targets.why: High massif with long sunlit periods and direct line of sight to Earth.

anchor.note: Approximate: IAU center of Mons Malapert.

targets.name: Mons Mouton and Mons Mouton Plateau
targets.why: Broad flat-topped massif; NASA lists both Mons Mouton and its plateau as candidate regions.

anchor.note: Approximate: IAU center of Mons Mouton; merges two NASA regions that share this anchor.

targets.name: Nobile rim
targets.why: Rim of Nobile crater; NASA lists two separate rim regions (Nobile Rim 1 and 2).

anchor.note: Approximate: ring on the rim of IAU crater Nobile (D = 79.3 km); merges Nobile Rim 1 and 2.

targets.name: de Gerlache rim
targets.why: Rim of de Gerlache crater, next to Shackleton; NASA region 'de Gerlache Rim 2'.

anchor.note: Approximate: ring on the rim of IAU crater de Gerlache (D = 32.7 km).

targets.name: Slater Plain
targets.why: Low-relief terrain around Slater crater close to the pole.

anchor.note: Approximate: IAU center of crater Slater; the NASA region is the plain around it.

targets.name: Peak near Cabeus B
targets.why: Elevated terrain next to Cabeus B, near the Cabeus cold trap where LCROSS detected water ice.

anchor.note: Approximate: ring on the rim of IAU crater Cabeus B (D = 59.6 km); the exact peak is not published.

targets.name: Shackleton rim
targets.why: Crater almost on the south pole; its rim has near-continuous sunlight and its floor is permanently shadowed.

anchor.note: Ring on the rim of IAU crater Shackleton (D = 20.9 km). Needs the polar patch support of T4.0.

targets.name: Jezero crater (Perseverance)
targets.why: Ancient lake delta; Perseverance is collecting samples for return to Earth.

targets.name: Gale crater (Curiosity)
targets.why: Crater with a layered sedimentary mound (Aeolis Mons) recording a long history of water.

targets.name: Gusev crater (Spirit)
targets.why: Basaltic plains with volcanic rocks; Spirit found evidence of past hydrothermal activity.

anchor.note: Columbia Memorial Station, IAU 2000 coordinates. TODO(verificar): fuente primaria (Parker et al. / Golombek et al.).

targets.name: Meridiani Planum (Opportunity)
targets.why: Very flat hematite-bearing plain; Opportunity found sedimentary rocks formed in water.

anchor.note: Challenger Memorial Station (354.4734 E), IAU 2000 areocentric.

targets.name: Utopia Planitia (Zhurong)
targets.why: Southern Utopia Planitia, a northern lowland plain with possible buried ice and mud features.

targets.name: Elysium Planitia (InSight)
targets.why: Chosen for being flat, smooth and low in rocks; the reference for safe, benign terrain.

targets.name: Oxia Planum (Rosalind Franklin)
targets.why: Clay-rich plain selected for ESA's ExoMars rover to search for signs of past life.

anchor.note: IAU center of Oxia Planum. TODO(verificar): center of the 2022 landing ellipse (ESA / Fawdon et al. 2024).

targets.name: Arcadia Planitia (shallow ice)
targets.why: Plains where SWIM maps find shallow, accessible water ice; a leading resource region for crewed missions.

anchor.note: Center of the SWIM Arcadia pilot-study figure (47.25 N, 196 E). It is a mapped region, not a landing site. TODO(verificar): figure in SWIM materials.
